title.narrative: Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future PLUS (O3 PLUS) Phase 2

description.narrative: Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future PLUS (O3 PLUS) Phase 2 project is scheduled for implementation from January 2026 to December 2029. O3 PLUS Phase 2 aims to transition from institution-specific interventions applied in the first phase to a national, system-wide implementation model in Zimbabwe. It will expand the programme reach to young people (aged 18-24 years old) in all 52 public HTEIs under the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and Technology Development (MoHTEISTD), including universities, polytechnics, industrial training colleges, and teachers’ training colleges. The programme will be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Entreprises Development (MWACSMED) and the MoHTEISTD across four strategic pillars: 1. Building Health Promoting Campuses: Institutionalization of student health and well-being across all institutions’ systems, governance, policy, leadership, and accountability structures. 2. Strengthening health systems within HTEIs: Build and strengthen the capacity of campus health facilities to offer youth-friendly health services for students, along with standardized referral pathways and support services as needed. 3. Safe and inclusive campus environments: Operationalize GBV policy and response mechanisms, enhance campus safety and inclusivity 4. Strengthen evidence‑based approaches and collaborative networks to enhance student health and well‑being: Digitize data management systems and enhance evidence generation and dissemination through collaborative networks By strengthening institutional capacities and aligning with national development frameworks, the programme aims to foster a network of health-promoting HTEIs that prioritize student and staff well-being and support the development of an empowered, healthy, and resilient generation of young people in Zimbabwe. This new phase will build on the momentum of Phase 1 and help shape a sustainable, nationwide impact.
